title: TS SDK: adapter patterns, Zod bootstrapping, JSON-Schema bridge, and streaming examples
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Teams using the TypeScript SDK struggle to wire model structured-output contracts into their apps without repeated runtime checks. Current patterns require either manual Zod schemas that drift from types or opaque JSON-Schema blobs for server-side validation. Streaming responses add a second axis of complexity: incremental validation, partial shape hints, and developer ergonomics for typed stream consumers.

Goal: Provide a set of adapter patterns and codegen primitives that let us: (1) generate discriminated-union TypeScript types and Zod validators from SDK output contracts, (2) emit an optional JSON-Schema bridge for external validation systems, (3) provide streaming parser helpers that validate incrementally and surface typed items in a friendly async-iterator API, and (4) ship a small set of examples/tutorials showing migration from manual validation to the generated flow.

Scope: This ticket implements the runtime adapters, the Zod helper factory, a light-weight JSON-Schema emitter, streaming parser utilities, and three end-to-end examples (chat tool-calling structured events, embeddings-batched metadata, and an ordered list discriminated union streamed from the model). It also includes unit tests, type tests, and docs for the SDK reference. Larger items (full CLI codegen and Go/Python parity) are out of scope for this ticket and will be tracked separately.
acceptance_criteria: Typegen: Given a simple output contract (union with discriminator), the codegen produces correct TypeScript types and a corresponding Zod schema factory (zodOfContract()) with runtime guards.
JSON-Schema bridge: zodOfContract().toJsonSchema() returns a JSON-Schema that round-trips against the Zod schema for basic constructs (objects, enums, discriminated unions, arrays).

Streaming ergonomics: an exported helper streamValidate<T>(stream, zodSchema) yields typed items as they are validated and surfaces validation errors tied to stream offsets without dropping the stream context.
Retries: SDK retry logic preserves idempotency metadata for structured output requests and replays partial KV-cache-safe prompts when safe; tests cover retryable vs non-retryable structured outputs.

Examples: at least three runnable TypeScript examples (in repo /examples/tsdk/structured-output/) demonstrating static validation, streaming validation, and JSON-Schema integration, each with README and automated smoke test.
Docs: API reference pages for the Zod helper, JSON-Schema bridge, and streaming helper are added to the SDK docs site with copy + small diagrams.
Quality: unit tests and type-level checks (tsd) pass in CI; PR contains changelog entry and migration notes.
Performance: streaming helper introduces <5% median latency overhead on end-to-end microbenchmarks vs raw stream iteration for typical 20–200 item streams.

notes:
Implementation notes and trade-offs captured in the design doc. Key trade-offs: (1) Keep Zod as first-class runtime validator because it composes well with existing TS types, (2) JSON-Schema emitter should be minimal to avoid tight coupling to AJV extensions, (3) streaming helper will validate chunks incrementally and buffer partial objects until a valid item completes; we will avoid expensive synchronous validation paths in the hot path, instead using scheduled microtasks where possible.

Performance targets: streaming overhead <5% median; typegen CI run time increase <10%.

Rollout plan: feature-flag the streamValidate API behind EXP_TS_OUTPUT_ADAPTERS; enable by default in tsdk-2.6 after a 2-week dogfood period.

Open Qs: how to represent backwards-compatible discriminator names in codegen (map vs preserve original), and whether to emit runtime metadata for stable contract versioning (proposal: include contractVersion string in generated schema).

release_notes: Add TypeScript SDK helpers for generating Zod validators from output contracts, an optional JSON-Schema bridge, and a streaming validation helper streamValidate that yields typed items during streaming. Includes migration examples and docs.
